newsitem.title: UKRAINE: AGROKHLEB-Ukraine harvest lags, yields/sunseed up.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Ukraine harvest lags, yields/sunseed up.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union, in association with Ukragroconsult, a private Ukrainian agricultural consultancy based in Kiev.
UKRAINE 1997 HARVESTING PROGRESS LAGS, BUT YIELDS RISE
KIEV, July 24 - Due to rainy weather, Ukraine's 1997 harvesting campaign has been much slower than last year's.
By July 15, 1.4 million hectares of cereals and pulses had been harvested, which was 57 percent down on last year's level.
However, average per-hectare yields are at 2.85 tonnes, compared to 1.96 tonnes, and one may expect yields to rise.
The Agriculture Ministry's net grain crop forecast is 38.2 million tonnes, including 34.3 million tonnes produced in the public sector and 3.9 million tonnes on private farms.
The updated estimate for sunseed plantings is 2.06 million hectares, which is 2.3 percent down on last year.
However, planting losses are expected to decline to 1.0-1.5 percent of the total crop, against 4.5 percent in 1996.
As a result, harvested sunseed acreage is likely to be 2.03-2.04 million hectares.
Assuming normal crop development, sunseed output is provisionally forecast rising to 2.65-2.75 million tonnes (1996: 2.10 million tonnes).
